item.title: DeLauro Eyes ICE Reform, Not Abolition
item.description: U.S. Rep. Rosa DeLauro emphasized her support on Friday for imposing “serious constraints” on Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) — and pushed back on calls from some local faith leaders to get rid of the agency altogether. The post DeLauro Eyes ICE Reform, Not Abolition appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Cold Couldn’t Stop Refugee Run
item.description: Eight-degree weather and below-zero windchill had nothing on New Haveners determined to support immigrants and refugees on Sunday morning. Nearly 1,800 people braved the cold to walk or run Integrated Refugee and Immigrant Services (IRIS)’ annual 5K “Run for Refugees” fundraiser in East Rock. Together, they raised over $100,000 for the organization. The post Cold Couldn’t Stop Refugee Run appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Let’s Go Swimming: An Argument For Building A Public Pool At English Station
item.description: (Opinion) It is almost perverse, given the sheer poundage of snow outside my house, to pick this moment to talk about swimming in the summer months. But because the city is currently deliberating plans to convert the former English Station power plant to a park that includes a swimming area, I say we dive in. The post Let’s Go Swimming: An Argument For Building A Public Pool At English Station appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Tenant, Face Of Affordable Housing Redev, Faces Eviction Lawsuit
item.description: In an Instagram video posted by Mayor Elicker to celebrate the opening of the Curtis Cofield II Estates, Reginald Blakey can be seen unlocking a front door, walking up a flight of steps, and standing in the kitchen of his new apartment. Eight months later, Blakey is on the receiving end of an eviction lawsuit. The post Tenant, Face Of Affordable Housing Redev, Faces Eviction Lawsuit appeared first on New Haven Independent.
